clue.text: "Every dog has his day" — including this wild one?

definitions.text: "Every dog has his day" — including this wild one?

parts.words: "Every dog has his day" — including this wild one?
parts.note: if every dog has its day, the wild dog of Africa and Asia must too, and its day is the one in Frederick Forsyth's thriller title The Day of the ...

explanation.surface: A proverb about everyone getting their turn, stretched to cover even a wild dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is the thriller and film The Day of the Jackal: this wild dog really does have its own day.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackal is a wild scavenging canine, so it is literally a wild dog that the proverb would include.

clue.text: Short girl crossing European river by a rosaceous shrub

indicators.note: the girl's clipped name spans the river, as a bridge crosses one
short means cut, so the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Janice is a girl's name
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A small girl crosses a river in Europe beside a flowering bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Japonica is a name for the Japanese quince, a flowering shrub of the rose family.

clue.text: Better covering for the head

explanation.surface: A better kind of headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Cap means to top or surpass, and also names a soft brimless hat.

clue.text: Ensign concerned with touring island group

indicators.note: going round, so the old preposition surrounds the islands

parts.note: anent is an old or Scots word meaning concerning
CI is the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: A naval junior officer is busy touring an archipelago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ensign' here is the old term for a flag or its bearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient is an archaic word for a standard or its bearer, as Iago is Othello's ancient.

clue.text: A couple of points established in successor's examination of feet

indicators.note: the point letters are set up inside the word for an heir, as something established in a place sits within it

parts.note: a scion is a descendant or heir, one who succeeds; the 's is read as 'is'
N and S are two compass points, north and south

explanation.surface: Reads like a medical heir checking a patient's feet, a chiropodist's inheritance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feet' are metrical feet in verse, not body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanning a line of poetry means marking out its metrical feet and stresses, which is exactly that analysis.

clue.text: Chatty fellow countryman digesting a lot of poetry

indicators.note: the countryman word takes the verse inside, as a stomach takes in food

parts.note: a conational is a citizen of the same nation

indicators.note: most but not all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: verse is poetry

explanation.surface: A talkative compatriot taking in a great deal of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A conversational style is chatty, informal and talky.

clue.text: Final release of vehicle trapped in blustery rain

indicators.note: the vehicle is caught inside the scrambled weather word
blustery weather is wild and tossed about, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A van stuck in a gusty downpour finally gets free.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism nirvana is the ultimate liberation from the cycle of rebirth.

clue.text: Type of injection sadly not universal — not quite

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone badly wrong, so the letters are rearranged
not quite means one short, so the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A kind of jab that is, unfortunately, not quite for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An intravenous injection is delivered straight into a vein, one type of injection.

clue.text: Small child — one with a bite!

definitions.meaning: an informal word for a young child
something that nips, like a crab or dog

explanation.surface: A toddler who bites.
explanation.definitionFit: Nipper is slang for a youngster and also literally anything that nips.

clue.text: Soldiers in Spanish port with share in renewal of energy

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
Vigo is a port in Galicia
a ration is an allotted share

explanation.surface: Troops in a Spanish harbour take their portion as energy returns.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinvigoration is the act of filling with vigour again, a restoring of energy.

clue.text: Smoker's requisite produced by daily on tube

indicators.note: in an across answer one word placed on another comes after it, so the cleaning lady follows the tube

parts.note: a pipe is a tube
a daily is a British cleaning woman who comes in each day

explanation.surface: An item a smoker needs, supposedly produced by a newspaper sitting on a tube train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like a newspaper; in Britain it is also a cleaner who comes in daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipe smokers use a fluffy wire stick to clear tar from the stem, an essential accessory.

clue.text: Most important vessel coming from the East

indicators.note: in an across answer travelling from the east means moving right to left, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pot is a vessel for cooking or holding liquid

explanation.definitionFit: Top in the sense of leading or foremost, as in top priority.

clue.text: Girl and boy wrapping last of durable fabric

parts.note: Nan is a girl's name

indicators.note: the boy's name surrounds the letter, as a wrapping goes round a parcel

parts.note: Ken is a boy's name

indicators.note: points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A girl and boy wrap themselves in the last of some hard-wearing cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nankeen is a yellowish cotton cloth, originally from Nanjing, so it is a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Magician in Tyneside clubs, one telling fanciful lies

parts.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, NE
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
a romancer embroiders or invents tales

explanation.surface: A conjuror working the Newcastle clubs who spins tall stories.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A necromancer is a sorcerer who claims to conjure the dead, a kind of magician.

clue.text: Female ultimately worried about male issue

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the final letter of the word before

parts.note: a man is a male
ate in the sense of troubled, as in 'what's eating you?'

explanation.surface: A woman who in the end got anxious about some man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is a link here: the pieces simply run E, MAN, ATE in order. 'Issue' is a verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To emanate is to flow out or come forth from a source, which is what issuing means.

clue.text: Party requisite causing agitation in Manhattan?

definitions.text: Party requisite causing agitation in Manhattan?

parts.words: Party requisite causing agitation in Manhattan?
parts.note: a Manhattan is a whisky and vermouth drink, so the agitation is mixing it, not unrest in New York

explanation.surface: Something at a party that stirs up trouble in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: Manhattan is the drink, not the borough.
explanation.definitionFit: A bar tool for shaking mixed drinks is a staple of parties and agitates a Manhattan cocktail.

clue.text: Alienate bishop leaving most agreeable mountain chain

parts.note: best means most pleasing
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a range is a line of mountains

explanation.surface: A bishop is driven off by leaving the loveliest mountains.

clue.text: Misses out, presumably, in these privileged occupations?

definitions.text: Misses out, presumably, in these privileged occupations?

parts.note: Misses are young women, who would be left out if the posts are kept for the lads

explanation.surface: Someone loses out on privileged posts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misses' looks like a verb (fails to get); it is the plural of Miss.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes cushy posts handed to friends and cronies, and literally excludes the women.

clue.text: Embrace monarch largely unknown in some quarters

indicators.note: the inner letters sit in between the two compass letters

parts.note: S and E are compass quarters, south and east

indicators.note: most of, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a queen is a monarch

explanation.surface: A sovereign mostly unrecognised but warmly hugged in certain areas.

clue.text: Sovereign English politician meets on ship

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
re means on or concerning
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: An English MP meets a ruler aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: An empress is a female sovereign ruling an empire.

clue.text: Disgusting old woman thus turning up outside university

parts.note: Di is a woman's name

indicators.note: the reversed word sits round the letter

clue.text: Way retired copper enters in manner of vampire

explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman; it is the metal.

clue.text: One resisting old person's first question

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling question

explanation.surface: Someone resisting an elderly person's opening question.

clue.text: Cetacean that kills seabird, by the sound of it

clue.text: Late 16th-century blaze in the area being developed

clue.text: Centre identified by married man dropping by

parts.note: hubby is an informal word for husband

explanation.surface: A focal point identified by a husband who popped in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping by' looks like visiting; here BY is dropped.

clue.text: NCO needing a lot of books after material
